title: Teh Tarik: Pulled, Frothy Malaysian Milk Tea
summary: Strong boiled black tea enriched with evaporated and condensed milk, then poured back and forth between jugs until thick, frothy and just cool enough to drink.
equipment: medium saucepan with a pouring lip
tea ball or tea filter bag
2 heatproof jugs or a second pan

ingredients.item: loose black tea, ideally Ceylon (or 3 tea bags)

steps.title: Brew
steps.text: Bring the water to the boil, add the tea in its filter and boil for 2-3 minutes, until deep amber. Boiling, rather than steeping, gives the strong brew the milk needs.

steps.title: Enrich
steps.text: Stir in the evaporated milk and 1 tbsp of the condensed milk and let it bubble gently for 2 minutes. Lift out the tea leaves.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Put 1 tbsp of condensed milk into each jug and divide the hot tea between them.

steps.title: Pull
steps.text: Working over the sink, pour one jug's tea into the other from about 15 cm, then pour it back. Repeat 4-6 times, raising the top jug a little each time once you feel confident. The long pour cools the tea slightly and whips it into a thick froth. Do the same with the second portion.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into the mugs with a head of foam on top. Taste and stir in a little more condensed milk if you like it sweeter.

tips: Practise the pull with cold water first.
Jugs with a pouring lip give a clean, thin stream.
Use Ceylon or a strong breakfast blend; delicate teas get lost under the milk.
storage: Best served immediately, while the froth is high. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
